title: Freezer sensor fault
shortDescription: The freezer compartment temperature sensor is out of range.
fullDescription:
E1 on a Bosch freezer means the compartment NTC sensor reads open or shorted, and the control cannot regulate temperature.

The compressor may keep running continuously until the sensor is repaired, which both wastes energy and risks freezing food solid.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 10 minutes and plug back in.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the rear panel in the freezer and install a new NTC sensor.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the evaporator is frosted over, indicating a defrost-system problem as well.

faq.a: Short-term yes, but replace the sensor within a few days.

title: Evaporator sensor fault
shortDescription: The evaporator coil sensor is not reading correctly.
fullDescription:
E2 means the sensor on the evaporator coil (used to end the defrost cycle) is open or shorted. Without it, the control either skips defrost or over-defrosts, leading to ice buildup or warm spells.

The fix is a sensor replacement behind the rear evaporator cover.

fixSteps.title: Defrost manually
fixSteps.instruction: Empty the freezer and let it thaw for 24 hours to clear any ice around the sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the evaporator cover and swap the coil NTC sensor.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if you are not comfortable removing the evaporator cover.

faq.a: No, ice around the sensor can keep the error latched.

title: Defrost heater fault
shortDescription: The defrost heater did not reach the expected temperature.
fullDescription:
E3 tells you the evaporator did not warm during a scheduled defrost cycle. Either the heater is open, the defrost thermostat is stuck open, or wiring to them is broken.

Left unfixed, the evaporator ices over and airflow collapses.

fixSteps.title: Defrost manually
fixSteps.instruction: Thaw the freezer overnight to clear ice from the coil.

fixSteps.title: Test heater
fixSteps.instruction: Measure the heater element for continuity; replace if open.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if you cannot safely access the heater behind the evaporator.

title: Evaporator fan fault
shortDescription: The evaporator fan is stalled or spinning too slow.
fullDescription:
E4 means the circulation fan in the freezer section is not spinning at the expected speed. Ice buildup on the blades, a seized motor, or a damaged harness are typical causes.

Without airflow, the freezer warms even though the compressor runs normally.

fixSteps.title: Thaw and inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Empty the freezer and let it defrost for 24 hours.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: If the fan does not spin freely, swap the motor.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the fan returns E4 after replacement; board drivers may be at fault.
videoSearchQuery: Bosch freezer E4 fan motor fix

faq.q: Can I leave the freezer running?
faq.a: Short-term only; inadequate airflow risks spoilage.

title: Door left open
shortDescription: The freezer door was open long enough to trigger a warning.
fullDescription:
E5 is a door-ajar alarm. The reed switch has reported the door open for longer than the allowed time, typically 2 minutes.

If the door is actually closed, the switch or magnet is at fault.

fixSteps.title: Close door firmly
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the door seals all the way around.

fixSteps.title: Check seal
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the gasket for tears and clean it with warm water.

fixSteps.title: Test switch
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the reed switch if the alarm sounds with the door fully closed.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro only if replacing the switch and gasket does not silence the alarm.
videoSearchQuery: Bosch freezer E5 door alarm fix

faq.a: Press the alarm button once to silence temporarily.

title: High compartment temperature
shortDescription: The freezer is warmer than the set point for too long.
fullDescription:
E6 warns that the freezer cannot reach its set temperature within a normal window. It often follows a long door-open event, a heavy load of unfrozen food, or a refrigeration system issue.

If temperature recovers within a few hours, no repair is needed.

fixSteps.title: Close and wait
fixSteps.instruction: Close the door and wait 6-8 hours for recovery.

fixSteps.title: Check seal
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the door gasket for tears or food debris.

repairTime: 10 minutes to check, hours to recover
whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the freezer does not recover after 12 hours with the door shut.

faq.a: Food still solidly frozen is safe; refreeze only cooked items.

title: Control board fault
shortDescription: The main control board reports an internal self-test failure.
fullDescription:
F1 is a firmware fault. The control board has failed its self-test and will not operate the compressor normally.

A full power reset sometimes clears transient F1 codes; repeat occurrences need a board replacement.

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 30 minutes and plug back in.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: Order a replacement main PCB and swap it.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the replacement board also shows F1.
videoSearchQuery: Bosch freezer F1 control board fix

faq.a: Yes, presets reset with a new board.

title: Compressor inverter fault
shortDescription: The variable-speed compressor is not starting or running correctly.
fullDescription:
F2 indicates the inverter board driving the compressor is not seeing the expected current draw. Bosch variable-speed compressors have a dedicated inverter that can fail independently of the main PCB.

The freezer will warm quickly while this fault is active.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: Book a technician to diagnose the compressor and inverter.

whenToCallPro: Always call a pro; sealed-system or compressor work needs certification.

faq.a: Yes, relocate it before it thaws.

title: Condenser fan fault
fullDescription:
F3 means the condenser fan at the bottom rear of the freezer has stopped or is running too slow. Dust bunnies are the most common cause; a failed motor the next.

Without this fan, the compressor overheats and shuts down on its internal thermal protector.

fixSteps.title: Clean coil and fan
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the freezer out and vacuum the condenser coil and fan blades.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the condenser fan motor if it does not spin freely.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if cleaning and a new motor do not clear F3.
videoSearchQuery: Bosch freezer F3 condenser fan fix

faq.q: How often should I clean the coil?
faq.a: Every 6 months, more often with pets.

title: Ambient sensor fault
shortDescription: The external ambient sensor is out of range.
fullDescription:
F4 means the sensor that measures kitchen temperature, used for adaptive defrost, is open or shorted. The freezer will fall back to a default defrost schedule, which is less efficient but still functional.

The sensor is usually mounted in the hinge or top of the cabinet.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Access the top hinge area and swap the ambient NTC.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if reaching the sensor requires removing the hinge assembly you are not familiar with.
videoSearchQuery: Bosch freezer F4 ambient sensor fix

faq.q: Is it worth fixing right away?
faq.a: Not urgent; the freezer still runs, just less efficiently.
